channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Swiss Franc strengthens as US Dollar falls on fading Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: USD/CHF depreciates after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around 0.8120 during the Asian hours on Wednesday. The pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) weakens amid easing expectations of a US interest rate hike next month.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Sits near three-week high, below $85.00 as bulls eye 100-SMA breakout
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – touches a nearly three-week high during the Asian session on Wednesday, though it struggles to build on the momentum beyond the $85.00 mark.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Wednesday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: UK CPI set to show inflation accelerated in July, bolstering case for BoE rate hike
item.description: The United Kingdom (UK) Office for National Statistics (ONS) will release the high-impact Consumer Price Index (CPI) report for July at 06:00 GMT.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Softens to near 184.50, mildly bearish bias persists under 100-day SMA
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross trades in negative territory around 184.60 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) edges higher against the Euro (EUR) amid hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens as Trump pauses 50% tariffs and USD slides before FOMC Minutes
item.description: The USD/CAD pair meets with fresh supply during the Asian session on Wednesday and, for now, seems to have stalled its recovery from the lowest level since June 3, touched earlier this week.

item.title: Gold recovers from weekly low as USD softens ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds from the weekly low, which it touched during the Asian session on Wednesday, and climbs above $4,350 in the last hour.

item.title: Australian Dollar weakens despite RBA’s Hauser hawkish remarks
item.description: AUD/USD extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 0.7080 during the Asian hours on Wednesday. Addressing the broader economic backdrop, Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser emphasized on Wednesday that inflation remains unacceptably high.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD extends decline to near $63 amid continued energy supply risks
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 0.5% to near $63.00 during the Asian trading session on Wednesday. The white metal extends its Tuesday’s decline amid fears of prolonged inflation concerns on the back of continued energy supply disruption.

item.title: US President Trump: I have paused 50% tariffs against Canada
item.description: Following overnight negotiations with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, US President Donald Trump announced on Wednesday, “I have paused 50% tariffs against Canada for a three-day period.”

item.title: RBA’s Hauser: Will have to raise rates again if inflation doesn’t come down
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said during the Asian trading session on Wednesday that inflation is too high and the central bank needs to raise interest rates to bring price pressures down.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains ground as BoJ rate hike bets rise
item.description: The USD/JPY pair edges lower to around 159.45 during the Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) as market expectations grow for another interest rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: United States Dollar Index hovers above 99.50 due to safe-haven support
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is steadying after registering minor gains in the previous day and trading around 99.60 during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines to weekly low as USD holds firm ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: The NZD/USD pair is seen extending this week's retracement slide from the 0.5925 area, or the highest since June 3, and drifting lower for the second straight day on Wednesday.

item.title: British Pound declines below 1.3550 on soft UK labour figures, traders brace for CPI data
item.description: The GBP/USD pair loses ground to around 1.3535 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The British Pound (GBP) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) amid disappointing UK labour data.

item.title: WTI rises to near $85.00 amid escalating US-Iran tensions
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price extends its gains for the fourth consecutive day, trading around $84.80 per barrel during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar consolidates near 1.3900 vs USD ahead of US tariffs deadline, FOMC Minutes
item.description: The USD/CAD pair struggles to capitalize on this week's modest recovery from its lowest level since June 3 and oscillates in a range around the 1.3900 mark during the Asian session on Wednesday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7854 vs. 6.7905 previous
item.description: On Wednesday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7854 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7905 and 6.7421 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro strengthens above 1.1550 on fading Fed hike bets
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades with mild gains near 1.1580 during the early Asian session on Wednesday. The US Dollar (USD) softens against the Euro (EUR) as softer US inflation data dialed back expectations of tighter Federal Reserve (Fed) policy.

item.title: Australian Dollar reverses as Iran risks lift USD ahead of Fed minutes
item.description: The Aussie Dollar reversed its course against the Greenback on Tuesday as investors remain uncertain of the outcome of the Middle East conflict, which tends to push energy prices higher, increasing the likelihood that major central banks would need to tighten monetary policy.

item.title: Trump, Carney hold last-minute talks ahead of new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney are negotiating in an effort to reach an agreement on tariffs, with just hours to go before the United States (US) imposes 50% tariffs on hockey sticks, wine and an array of other Canadian imports, CNBC reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold steadies below $4,350 as surging yields offset support from Fed rate-hold bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) holds steady near $4,335 after pulling back from an early-June top near $4,450 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The precious metal faced some selling pressure in the previous session as Treasury yields surged to their highest levels in decades.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: SMAs confluence blocks bulls near 185.00
item.description: The EUR/JPY registers two consecutive days of gains, but on Tuesday, buyers failed to gain traction as they faced a confluence of key resistance levels near the 184.70 area. The cross-pair is poised to end the day unchanged, near its opening price of 184.69.

item.title: The Japanese Yen gives back half a record intervention
item.description: The Dollar trades near 159.50 against the Yen on Tuesday after a session high just short of 160.00, the strongest level the pair has reached since Tokyo and Washington intervened together at the end of July.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls stall near 216.00 as RSI flattens
item.description: The GBP/JPY consolidates at familiar levels on Tuesday, virtually unchanged near 216.00, with the cross-pair seesawing within the 215.85-216.22 range, as neither buyers nor sellers are able to clear key resistance/support levels during the day.

item.title: British Pound Sterling's three-month high was made in America
item.description: The British Pound trades just short of 1.3550 against the Dollar on Tuesday, holding inside Monday's range after a peak short of 1.3600 carried it to its strongest level since early May. That leaves close to 300 pips of recovery from the base just short of 1.3300 built in the first week of August.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds steady amid a firm US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD hovers around the 0.5870 zone at the time of writing on Tuesday, marginally lower on the day. The pair is treading water as a firm US Dollar (USD) and a cautious market mood keep the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) on the back foot.

item.title: US President Trump says no Iran talks; naval blockade remains
item.description: The US President Donald Trump posted on his social network that “there are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect. The Hormuz Strait is open and operating.

item.title: Mexican Peso dips on Middle East tensions, eyes on FOMC minutes
item.description: The Mexican Peso loses some ground on Tuesday, depreciating by about 0.16% against the US Dollar as investors await the release of the Federal Reserve’s last meeting minutes, with a resolution of the US-Iran conflict remaining unlikely.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Sideways range holds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH has been trading quietly, with intraday ranges clustered around current levels.
